h: Battersea treetop tips and park extras
p: Expect your Go Ape adventure to take a good couple of hours or more on the course, plus time to check in and get through the safety briefing. Instructors fit your harness and teach you how to clip on and off, then keep an eye from the ground while you make your way round. That makes the briefing important, so listen up.

Younger participants need a participating adult alongside them, with set ratios depending on ages, so check what's required for your group when you book. Wear trainers or walking shoes with grip and comfortable clothes you can stretch in.

Getting there is easy. Battersea Park station is just south of the park, Queenstown Road is close by too, and the Northern line's Battersea Power Station stop is a short walk away. Buses run along the edges of the park, and the riverside path brings you in from Chelsea and Albert Bridge.

The rest of the park has lots to offer. Battersea Park Children's Zoo is a small, friendly zoo that's ideal for younger kids who aren't old enough for the treetops. There are tennis courts, sports pitches and wide open lawns for a picnic, and in the warmer months you can hire boats on the lake. Albert Bridge, lit up after dark, is one of the prettiest sights on the Thames.
